status: Filed BEFORE any Phase-2 policy was trained and before any Phase-2 cell existed. Additive: the parent is not rewritten. No decision rule, threshold, endpoint, arm definition or prediction is changed. The parent's own amendment_rule requires this record because a pinned code file changed.

corrections.reason: Refuse consolidation_fraction > 0 on the gate and ramp modes. Consolidation pins every cohort at lambda = 1.0 for the final stretch of training; for an arm whose frontier ends at 1.5 that is a support CONTRACTION, applied silently and invisible to the gate's incident log because the gate never requested it. It would have falsified the arm's central safety claim with nothing in the telemetry to show it.
corrections.behavioural_effect_on_phase_2: NONE. Neither gate_150 nor ramp_150 sets consolidation_fraction; the launcher passes it for no expansion arm. The change converts an unreachable-but-latent hazard into a construction-time refusal. Every other code path is byte-identical.

corrections.target: design.max_delay (was 14), arms.gate_150.probe_max (was 2.0), and the probe's maximum applied intensity
corrections.defect: The probe stratum was allowed to sit one step above the frontier without a ceiling, so a gate or ramp arm at frontier 1.5 would apply lambda 1.625 in its probe cohort. fixed_150 and fixed_u150 top out at 1.5. The expansion arms would therefore have trained on strictly MORE support than the arms they are compared against, and a win would have been confounded with a support difference -- the same class of error as reading the ratchet's difficulty increase as a method effect.
corrections.discovered_by: a dry run of the full five-arm launch, which fixed_u150's frozen delay contract refused at --max-delay 14
corrections.correction: The probe is capped at the frontier ceiling: gate_probe_max = 1.5 for both expansion arms. Maximum applied intensity is now exactly 1.5 for all four 1.5 arms. At the ceiling the probe stratum becomes a second frontier stratum, which is harmless because the gate has stopped expanding. --max-delay for the campaign changes from 14 to 12, which is also fixed_u150's frozen requirement.
corrections.note: Filed before any Phase-2 policy was trained. No endpoint, threshold, decision rule or prediction changes; the comparison becomes cleaner, not easier.

corrections.target: how a stalled gate is read, and what is done about it
corrections.finding: A feasibility replay of the frozen gate law over the real per-iteration time-out series of fixed@s8600 (receipts/analysis/lucid_gate_feasibility_20260901.json, tools/simulate_gate.py) shows the gate's trajectory is highly sensitive to how much harder the probe is than the frontier. At the frozen threshold 0.80 it reaches 1.5 by iteration ~3,500 only if the probe is as easy as the frontier, which it never is; under a 5-point-per-step penalty it stalls at 1.375, and under 12 points at 1.125. This is a PROXY, not a prediction: the series is a fixed-DR arm's population rate and the penalty model is invented.
corrections.threshold_NOT_changed: The frozen threshold stays 0.80. It was chosen a priori as 'the probe should be surviving most of its episodes before we widen', and re-tuning it against a proxy simulation built to make the arm expand is precisely the post-hoc adjustment this programme exists to avoid.
interpretation_rule: If gate_150 reaches 1.5 and still loses to ramp_150 on the primary, D2 fails on its merits: the feedback rule bought nothing that a schedule did not, at equal terminal support.

If gate_150 STALLS below 1.5, it necessarily trains on less support than ramp_150, so a loss on the primary is expected and is NOT evidence that feedback is useless. It is evidence that this threshold was too conservative for this task. D2 still records a fail -- the rule is not revised -- but the report must state which of the two cases occurred, because they license different next steps.
A stall is never repaired by lowering the threshold and rerunning the same seed.
corrections.zero_gpu_followup: gate_150 records probe survival every iteration in survival_<branch>.jsonl, so the gate law can be replayed against the ACTUAL probe series at any threshold for no GPU cost: tools/simulate_gate.py --survival-jsonl <path> --thresholds ... . That measures how conservative 0.80 was on real data and fixes the threshold for a second seed on evidence rather than on a guess. This analysis is authorized in advance and its result may set the threshold for Phase 3, but it may NOT revise any Phase-2 decision.

corrections.target: the PRIMARY endpoint's threshold justification (parent: 'SD 0.0221, so 0.05 is about 2.3 SD')
corrections.defect: The parent justified the +0.05 threshold using the identical-exposure noise cluster's SD of 0.0221. The H_R2 readout of 2026-09-01 16:08 supplies something better: three genuinely PAIRED ratchet-minus-fixed deltas on the exact {phys_175, phys_200} band, from three training seeds on the same instrument.

measured.endpoint: mean success on phys_175 and phys_200, equal weight

corrections.consequence: The frozen +0.05 threshold is 1.83 SD of a measured paired delta, not the 2.3 SD the parent claimed. A 2.3-SD threshold on this endpoint would be 0.063. The screen therefore has LESS power than preregistered, and a single-seed pass at 0.05-0.06 is weaker evidence than the parent's wording implies.
corrections.threshold_NOT_changed: 0.05 stays. Raising it after seeing a noise estimate would be as much a post-hoc adjustment as lowering it, and the parent's rule forbids revising thresholds. What changes is the STRENGTH claimed for a pass, which is a reporting obligation, not a decision rule.
corrections.reporting_obligation: Any Phase-2 result at or near the threshold must be reported as ~1.8 SD of the measured paired noise, explicitly, and must not be described as clearing a 2.3-SD bar. Phase 3 multi-seed confirmation is mandatory before ANY directional language, which the parent already required and this measurement reinforces.
corrections.related_finding: The between-seed effect on absolute capability is large and is not the arm: pooling both arms, seed means of frontier success AUC are 0.904 (8600), 0.898 (8601), 0.826 (8602), so seed 8602 sits ~7.8 pts below the others for BOTH arms. Pooled six-arm SD 4.0 pts, range 9.3 pts.
corrections.data_driven_note: This correction IS data-driven, unlike A1-A4, but the data is from a DIFFERENT and already-decided experiment (H_R2), not from any Phase-2 cell. No Phase-2 policy has been trained. It changes no threshold and no decision rule; it corrects a power claim.

corrections.reason: Added a docstring section recording that the gate's signal has AUTHORITY, not merely anchoring: the actuator moves probe survival, and in the direction that withholds the next expansion. It also records the measured r(lambda, gap) = -0.201 that explains why the observed evacuations are total rather than partial.
corrections.behavioural_effect_on_phase_2: NONE, and this was verified rather than asserted. Parsing both revisions and removing every module, class and function docstring yields byte-identical ASTs (257940cf45fdc9cf both sides). The change is documentation only.

corrections.reason: The gate arm now aborts if no probe episode arrives within a grace period past warm-up. Phase 2 is the first live run of survival_observer, and a dead signal path produces an applied-lambda trace identical to an honest decision not to expand. Because amendment A4 preregisters a stall as a legitimate result, a broken wire would have been read as evidence about feedback. Mechanism gate G3 catches it only after a full 8,000-iteration cell.
corrections.behavioural_effect_on_phase_2: Adds an abort path that fires ONLY when the gate has received zero probe episodes for gate_evidence_grace=200 iterations past warm-up. A single probe episode satisfies it permanently, so sparse evidence is unaffected. It cannot fire on ramp_150, which reads nothing, nor on any fixed arm. It cannot change any expansion decision: it either raises or does nothing.
corrections.interaction_with_A4: A4 says a stalled gate is a result, not a failed screen. A7 narrows that: a stall is a result only when the gate was actually receiving evidence. A stall with zero probe episodes is now a fault that aborts, and can no longer be mistaken for a decision.

corrections.defect: The survival gate's probe strata were never bound to the observer. Callback order is dict order in the Hydra config and the curriculum's on_train_begin runs BEFORE the survival observer's, so at _bind time the observer had not registered itself, the lookup returned None, and set_strata was never called. The observer then recorded only population survival, current_probe returned no evidence for the whole run, and the gate held its frontier at 1.0 forever.
corrections.why_it_matters: This is the most expensive possible false negative. In the applied-lambda trace a gate that never received evidence is indistinguishable from a gate that honestly decided not to expand, so it would have been read as evidence against feedback when nothing had been measured. It would also have satisfied amendment A4's 'a stalled gate is a result' reading, which is exactly wrong for a fault.
corrections.discovered: Three minutes into the first Phase-2 launch (experiment lucid_support_expansion_ne1024_20260901_232033), by inspecting the observer's own jsonl rather than trusting the curriculum's survival_observer_present flag. The two files contradicted each other: the curriculum logged survival_observer_present true with correct 8-stratum TACE telemetry and sizes [43,43,43,43,42,42,640,128], while the observer's rows carried probe_index null and no per-stratum entry.
corrections.caught_by: Manual inspection. The fail-fast guard added in 08a01bf WOULD have aborted the arm at iteration 210, about two minutes later, so the guard worked; the run was stopped early to fix the root cause rather than to let the arm die.
corrections.correction: Strata are bound lazily, the first time the observer is reachable, in _survival_observer. Regression test TestLateObserverRegistration reproduces the ordering and fails on the parent commit.
corrections.run_status: The aborted experiment lucid_support_expansion_ne1024_20260901_232033 is VOID and is retained as excluded evidence. Its gate_150 cell reached ~46 iterations. No Phase-2 cell has been scored and no endpoint, threshold, decision rule or prediction changes.

The paused trainer holds ~6.7 GiB of GPU memory throughout, so the prototype arms train under memory contention, which affects their wall-clock only.
